goal: Make per-ask Ask regeneration reachable for the owner on a built Solicitation batch — a route, a per-ask control with its 3/day budget counter — and close #629 deviation D3 by refusing regeneration once Owner approval is recorded, so "what was approved is byte-for-byte what sends" becomes unconditional.
non_goals: Owner editing of a rendered ask — D22 stands, and the panel must keep saying so
Post-approval regeneration in any form, including a per-ask re-approval state machine (this is the decision, not a deferral)

"Regenerate all" — spec §8.2 r1 calls it a #629 UI affordance, but the outbox dedup is keyed (topic, aggregate_id = batchId), so a fan-out of N enqueues 1 and silently drops N−1; structurally impossible without re-keying the dedup
Any change under worker/ — worker/jobs/solicitation-batch/generate.ts already dispatches on ask_id
The admin/support halt surface (admin_halt remains a CHECK member with no writer)
Flipping SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED in any environment — blocked on #633, and the boot assert would crash the staging worker
user_visible_behavior: On a built, ready batch the owner sees a Regenerate control on every rendered ask, with "N of 3 today" beside it
Clicking it rewrites that one message; the row shows it is being rewritten, and the new copy replaces it in place when it lands
The control is absent on held-back asks, and disabled on asks the owner has deselected and on asks that have spent their 3/day budget
While a rewrite is in flight, Approve and every other Regenerate control are disabled
Once the batch is approved, no Regenerate control exists anywhere and a direct POST is refused
The approvable-mode copy reads "You can ask for a new version of any message, but you cannot write one yourself."
When a rewrite settles without changing the copy (a worker-side refusal), the panel says so rather than silently showing the same text
invariants: Byte-for-byte approval is UNCONDITIONAL: once approved_at is set, no path may replace a rendered ask's bytes — regenerateAsk refuses in every state except built
Transactional outbox (#2): the ask_regeneration_requested run step and the job_outbox row are written in ONE Postgres transaction
Tenant isolation (#8): every read and write carries both account_id and business_id; a bare batch or ask id is no tenant proof
Domain modules receive sql explicitly (#15); the route is the composition root
Feature flags are server-authoritative (#13): no NEXT_PUBLIC companion; the browser learns send-lane state from the response shape alone
D6a redaction: a moderation_high attempt never gains a regenerate control, because toRows never turns it into a row
Spec §8.2 r6: a withheld (blocked) ask is terminal for the batch and is never regenerable
Cost-guard direction: the advisory peek fails OPEN; the worker's Lua INCR (checkAskRegenBudget) stays the authoritative gate
At most one regeneration is in flight per batch — the (topic, aggregate_id) partial unique index owns that fact
edge_cases: Owner clicks regenerate, then approves before the worker swaps: approval succeeds, the swap's locked re-check refuses, the spend is discarded and approved bytes are untouched. The panel disables Approve while regeneratingAskId is non-null to make this rare rather than to rely on it

A regenerate mints a NEW outreachId, so a stale id in the panel's exclusion set would fail the whole approval unknown_exclusion (fail-closed). The exclusion set must be pruned to ids still present in sendable on every refetch
A regenerated replacement is itself withheld: the ask ends with no live render, closeBatchIfSettled may settle the batch, and the panel flips to nothing_to_send or settled
Budget exhausted between the advisory peek and the worker's INCR: the worker refuses, the outbox row completes, the copy is unchanged, and the panel detects it by comparing attemptNo
Redis unavailable: the peek resolves to an empty map, no counter renders and every control stays enabled; the worker still refuses over-budget work
Two tabs: tab B's control is disabled by the server-authoritative regeneratingAskId, and a race that gets past it answers 409 already_in_flight
A whole-batch generation row is in flight: its payload has no ask_id, so regeneratingAskId is null and the panel is in preparing mode with no controls at all
An ask id belonging to another batch or another tenant answers the uniform 404, indistinguishable from an unknown one
SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED off: the route 404s and the panel renders no control, because sendLane is null
A rendered outreach row implies a send parent run, so a null parent is an impossible state and throws with context rather than branching (regenerateAsk's own precedent)

rollback_plan: No migration, so rollback is a plain revert of the PR: the regenerate route disappears and REGENERABLE_BATCH_STATES returns to its four-state form. SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED is off in every environment, so neither the shipped state nor the reverted state is reachable by any customer. Order: revert on main, then re-sync staging to main per deployment-guide.md §Re-sync staging.
observability: New route log ask_regeneration_requested (ids and counts only, never rendered subject or body) plus the matching run step on the send parent
Existing worker lines [AskRegeneration] "ask regenerated" and "ask regeneration refused" with their reason field — the refusal vocabulary is how a silent no-op is diagnosed
